name: D. James Kennedy
role: Presbyterian pastor, broadcaster, founder of Evangelism Explosion, and Christian Right leader

died.cause: Heart failure, months after a cardiac arrest in December 2006

summary: Founding pastor of Coral Ridge Presbyterian Church in Fort Lauderdale, whose Evangelism Explosion method trained millions in personal evangelism and whose broadcasts and organizations made him a leading voice of the Christian Right.

key_dates.label: Converted after hearing a radio sermon by Donald Grey Barnhouse, while working as a dance instructor
Founding pastor of Coral Ridge Presbyterian Church, Fort Lauderdale
Begins the lay-training program that becomes Evangelism Explosion
Launches The Coral Ridge Hour on television
Publishes What If Jesus Had Never Been Born? with Jerry Newcombe
Founds the Center for Reclaiming America

accomplishments.text: Built Coral Ridge Presbyterian Church from a handful of members in 1959 into one of the largest Presbyterian congregations in the United States; it later joined the Presbyterian Church in America.
Developed Evangelism Explosion, a method of training church members to share their faith using two diagnostic questions; it spread to churches in every country in the world.
Reached millions through The Coral Ridge Hour television program and Truths That Transform radio broadcast.
Founded Westminster Academy (1971), Knox Theological Seminary (1989), the Center for Christian Statesmanship in Washington (1995), and the Center for Reclaiming America (1996).

Served on the board of the Moral Majority and campaigned against abortion and homosexuality and for the view that America was founded as a Christian nation; critics, including Americans United for Separation of Church and State, opposed his political activism.
His Center for Reclaiming America sponsored the 1998 'Truth in Love' newspaper campaign promoting the claim that gay people could change their orientation, which was widely criticized.
His ministry's 2006 documentary Darwin's Deadly Legacy, linking Darwin's theory to Nazism, was condemned by the Anti-Defamation League as trivializing the Holocaust.

sayings_intro: The two questions at the heart of Evangelism Explosion.

original.phrase: Have you come to a place in your spiritual life where you know for certain that if you were to die today you would go to heaven?
Suppose you were to die today and stand before God and He were to say to you, 'Why should I let you into My heaven?' What would you say?

persecution_note: Kennedy was never arrested or persecuted. His political activism drew strong public criticism from civil-liberties, gay-rights, and Jewish organizations.
excommunication_note: Kennedy was never excommunicated or disciplined by any church.

sources.citation: D. James Kennedy, Evangelism Explosion. Wheaton, IL: Tyndale House, 1970 (4th ed., 1996).
